title: Slingshot
teaches: The Slingshot as we trade it: a leader that just had a drive pulls back a few closes under the 4-day EMA of the highs, orderly and shallow, and the buy is the first decisive close back over that line, never the gap day and never the guess at the low; the stop sits a few cents under the trigger day's low, a third comes off at 3R and 5R with the rest on the trail, and a loss taken at the stop is the system working.

facts.quote: Slingshot =  c > xavgh4 and c1 < xavgh4.1 and c2 < xavgh4.2 and c3 < xavgh4.3
facts.claim: Scot1and's own scan: the close over the 4-period EMA of the highs after the three prior closes under it.

facts.quote: a 4EMA of the HIGHS
facts.claim: Scot1and's line is a 4-period EMA of the highs.

facts.quote: This setup is to target a reversal of a shallow pull back.
facts.claim: Scot1and: the setup targets the reversal of a shallow pullback.

facts.quote: The theory behind this setup is that we take a powerful stock and stretch it with pull back.  Then when momentum resumes we enter.
facts.claim: Scot1and: take a powerful stock, let a pullback stretch it, and enter when momentum resumes.

facts.quote: The resumption of the momentum for the slingshot is triggered by the break of the 4EMA of the HIGHS.
facts.claim: Scot1and: the trigger is the break of the 4-period EMA of the highs.

facts.quote: Power can be found using a variety of scans.  52 Week high, RSI, High OBV, high Mdt.  High RS compared to the S&P.
facts.claim: Scot1and finds power with strength scans, including high relative strength against the S&P.

facts.quote: After the Slingshot shoots, the EMA 4 should never be breached on a close.  Consider it the trailing stop on the position.
facts.claim: Scot1and's own trail: a close under the EMA 4; not ours.

facts.quote: My Slingshot indicator is simply a 4EMA of the highs.
facts.claim: Scot1and's write-up: the indicator is a 4EMA of the highs.

facts.quote: First, there must be upward momentum. A pull back in a stock in a downtrend is merely an opportunity to sell into strength.
facts.claim: Scot1and: upward momentum first; a pullback in a downtrend is a chance to sell, not to buy.

facts.quote: Tight trading ranges before the trigger are ideal for two reasons. It signals that the selling pressure is waning and perhaps, more importantly, it permits very tight stops.
facts.claim: Scot1and: tight ranges before the trigger show selling pressure fading and allow very tight stops.

facts.quote: I typically place my stop at the low of the slingshot day. Or at most, the bottom of the consolidation period. Stops should be tight, much tighter than a breakout.
facts.claim: Scot1and: the stop is the low of the slingshot day, or at most the bottom of the consolidation.

facts.quote: Ideally, we want to find a stock that has recently made a strong move.
facts.claim: Scot1and: find a stock that has recently made a strong move.

facts.quote: The advantage of the setup is that it provides a low risk entry with a tight stop.
facts.claim: Scot1and: the setup's advantage is a low-risk entry with a tight stop.

facts.quote: The Slingshot setup, developed by Scot1and, is a strategy designed to capitalize on entering powerful stocks immediately after a pullback.
facts.claim: Deepvue: Scot1and's Slingshot enters powerful stocks right after a pullback.

facts.quote: This setup is characterized by the price crossing above the high of the 5-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA) from the period under analysis.
facts.claim: Deepvue describes a 5-day EMA; a dissent from the originator's 4.

facts.quote: The stop loss is at the low of the slingshot indicator trigger bar, so we want consolidation as it lowers the amount of risk on the trade.
facts.claim: Analyzing Alpha: the stop is the low of the trigger bar, so a tight consolidation lowers the risk.

facts.quote: The slingshot indicator, which is a component of the slingshot setup, fires when the current bar’s close crosses the 4-ema of the highs.
facts.claim: Analyzing Alpha: the indicator fires when the close crosses the 4-period EMA of the highs.

facts.quote: Scot1and developed the slingshot setup to get into a powerful stock after a pullback just as the downward momentum stops and the stock begins to go back up.
facts.claim: Analyzing Alpha: the Slingshot gets into a powerful stock after a pullback, as the downward momentum stops.

facts.quote: That logically makes our stop the low of entry day.
facts.claim: Bonde: the stop is the low of the entry day.

facts.quote: Stop first (by default a few cents under the day's low or the prior day's low, F62); the size comes from the stop; if the honest stop does not fit the risk, skip the trade.
facts.claim: A3: stop first; the size comes from the stop; if the honest stop does not fit, skip.

facts.quote: The stop is the exit. It only moves up, never down or wider. The one exception is the gap rule (B20).
facts.claim: A4: the stop is the exit; it only moves up; the gap rule is the one exception.

facts.quote: Shares = account × risk % ÷ (entry − stop), rounded down, then capped: the size is the SMALLER of the risk-based size and the position cap
facts.claim: A5: shares are account times risk percent, divided by entry minus stop, rounded down, then capped.

facts.quote: The full size at one price with one stop; no adding.
facts.claim: A5: full size at one price with one stop; no adding.

facts.quote: "I almost never take a loss greater than 3%": the stop usually sits within about 3% of the buy (a loss on the position, not the account).
facts.claim: A13: the stop usually sits within about 3% of the buy.

facts.quote: Move the stop to breakeven at 2R to 5R, ideally. The first trim: the hard rule is a third at 3R; ideally anywhere from 3R to 6R, and in practice he mostly waits for 5R.
facts.claim: B19: breakeven between 2R and 5R; the hard rule for the first trim is a third at 3R.

facts.quote: A gap against the stop: the first 30 minutes of the gap-down day decide. The low of the first 30-minute bar is the new stop.
facts.claim: B20: on a gap through the stop, the first 30-minute low is the new stop.

facts.quote: With a ceiling: if the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R, get out.
facts.claim: B20's ceiling: past 2R in the first 30 minutes, get out.

facts.quote: No new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report; hold through a report only if the trade is up 5R.
facts.claim: B22: no new buys in the 3 days before a report; hold through one only if up 5R.

facts.quote: Trade only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day.
facts.claim: B23: only stocks at $10 or more trading at least $20 million a day.

facts.quote: The 200-day line: no longs below the 200-day simple moving average, unless it is a parabolic long; shorts only below the 200-day, never above it unless it is a parabolic short.
facts.claim: B26: no longs below the 200-day simple moving average, except a parabolic long.

facts.quote: No chasing: never buy more than 4% above the buy point.
facts.claim: C28: never buy more than 4% above the buy point.

facts.quote: Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays under the buy point, so the distance grows and the shares shrink (A5).
facts.claim: C28: chasing costs size, because the stop stays put and the distance grows.

facts.quote: Too stretched to buy: skip a long that is more than 10% above its 10-day average.
facts.claim: C29: skip a long more than 10% above its 10-day average.

facts.quote: Buy leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups, except parabolic and mean-reversion trades.
facts.claim: C31: buy leaders, an RS rating of 80 or more in a strong group.

facts.quote: Time stop: a trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money.
facts.claim: C33: a trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold.

facts.quote: A climax run on your own long (Bracco's parabolic burst): sell a big part into it, a judgment call.
facts.claim: C34: sell a big part into a climax run, a judgment call.

facts.quote: We swing trade: days to a few weeks; a winner can be held longer while it keeps working.
facts.claim: C35: we swing trade; a winner can be held longer while it keeps working.

facts.quote: Every position has a real stop order with the broker, not a stop kept in your head.
facts.claim: D41: a real stop order with the broker.

facts.quote: Never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume; illiquid stocks are not even watched.
facts.claim: D42: never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume.

facts.quote: After the first third at 3R: another third at 5R, then trail the last third; adjustable.
facts.claim: E51: another third at 5R, then trail the last third.

facts.quote: Default trail: the 10-day average for fast movers, the 21-day for steadier ones; sell on a close below it.
facts.claim: E52: trail the 10-day for fast movers, the 21-day for steadier ones; sell on a close below it.

facts.quote: Entries are market orders.
facts.claim: E57: entries are market orders.

facts.quote: The stop sits a few cents under the day's low, not exactly on it.
facts.claim: F62: the stop sits a few cents under the day's low.

facts.quote: If a stock opens above a trim level (3R, 5R), take that trim at the open.
facts.claim: F63: a trim level the day opens past is taken at the open.

facts.quote: The market reading as a guide (A10): Green, full risk per grade and up to 10 positions; Yellow, smaller and fewer; Orange, only A+ setups; Red, mostly cash and shorts.
facts.claim: F65: Green full risk; Yellow smaller and fewer; Orange only A+; Red mostly cash and shorts.

facts.quote: After a stop-out, buy again only if the setup triggers again, as a new trade with its own stop and every rule.
facts.claim: B21: after a stop-out, buy again only on a new trigger, as a new trade.

facts.quote: The same stock: at most 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month.
facts.claim: E56: at most 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month on one stock.

facts.quote: Setup grades set the size: A and B setups at normal size; A+ sized up; B- or lower sized down.
facts.claim: D38: A and B normal size; A+ sized up; B- or lower sized down.

facts.claim: D44: no setup, no trade; cash is a position.

facts.claim: E49: risk by grade; B- or lower 0.25% to 0.5%.

walkthroughs.title: UTHR, September 2025: the textbook Slingshot
steps: UTHR, September 2025. A 37.7% news gap on 2025-09-02 is the drive. Three tiny red days hug the line.
Context holds: above its 50-day and 200-day, 9.3% deep, orderly at 0.45 ATR.

questions.q: A stock gaps up 18% on earnings and closes over the 4-day EMA of highs that same day. Is that the Slingshot trigger?
choices: No; the gap day is not the trigger
Yes; the close is over the line
Yes, if volume is heavy on the gap
No; the trigger is the first red day
questions.answer: No; the gap day is not the trigger
questions.why: No. The drive day is never the trigger. If the only qualifying drive day is the trigger day itself, it is not a Slingshot. The trigger is the first daily close above the line after a pullback of at least 3 closes under it. An 18% gap or heavy volume does not change that order. Scot1and: take a powerful stock, stretch it with a pullback, then enter when momentum resumes.
questions.lesson_line: The gap is the engine. The Slingshot is the pullback after it, never the gap day itself.

wrong.Yes; the close is over the line: A close over the line on the drive day is the drive, not a trigger. Nothing has pulled back yet.
wrong.Yes, if volume is heavy on the gap: Volume does not turn a gap day into a Slingshot. The order is drive, pullback, then the close back over.
wrong.No; the trigger is the first red day: Buying the first red day of the pullback instead of waiting for the close back over the line is a named mistake. The trigger is the first daily close above the line after the pullback.

questions.simple: No, because the gap day is the drive, and the trigger only comes after a pullback and a close back over the line.

deeper.trap: The gap day looks perfect: a big green bar and a close over the line. That is why it fools people. Before you call anything a trigger, count the closes under the line. With none, there was no pullback, so there is no Slingshot yet.

questions.simple: False. The stop goes a few cents under the low of the trigger day, not the low of the drive day.

questions.q: By our card, where does a decisive Slingshot trigger day close within its range?

Just over the line is enough
In the bottom 30%, a shakeout
Right at the middle, the 50% mark

A 3 ATR range, two gap days

questions.q: Our card's wider stop choice for a Slingshot sits where?
choices: Under the lower of two days' lows
Well under the pullback low, for safety
Under the 50-day moving average
A full ATR under the trigger low
questions.answer: Under the lower of two days' lows

questions.lesson_line: Wider means the lower of two days' lows. The pullback's bottom is the outer limit.

wrong.A full ATR under the trigger low: The card's wider choice is still a few cents under a low, not an ATR below one.
wrong.Well under the pullback low, for safety: The wider choice is never wider than the bottom of the pullback. Going well under it is not on the card.
wrong.Under the 50-day moving average: An average is not a low. The stop is a few cents under a day's low.

questions.simple: The wider choice puts the stop a few cents under the lower of the trigger day's and the prior day's lows.

deeper.trap: Wider does not mean as wide as you like. The card's wider choice is the lower of two days' lows, and it is never wider than the bottom of the pullback. A wider stop costs size, because the shares come from account risk divided by the distance to the stop.

A Slingshot

Yes; first red day is the entry
Yes; buy half now, half later

Sell half and hold the rest

questions.why: Sell before the report. We hold through a report only if the trade is up 5R, and this one is up 1.5R. A rally Slingshot near a report is the case that binds. A PEG Slingshot is usually weeks from the next one. A gap through the stop is handled by the gap rule, which has a 2R ceiling.
questions.lesson_line: Earnings is a gap you cannot stop. Five R buys the ticket; 1.5R does not.

wrong.Hold; the trend is up, so it is fine: The trend is not the test. The rule holds through a report only at 5R, and this trade is up 1.5R.
wrong.Sell half and hold the rest: The rest would still be held through the report at 1.5R. The rule needs 5R for that.
wrong.Hold; the stop covers a report gap: A stop does not cover a gap. Price can open through it, and then the gap rule takes over with its 2R ceiling.

questions.story: Your rally Slingshot is up 1.5R. The report comes after the close in two sessions.
questions.simple: Sell, because we hold through a report only if the trade is up 5R, and this one is up just 1.5R.

deeper.trap: Up 1.5R feels like a cushion, but the rule sets a high bar, 5R, to hold through a report. Even the gap rule has a ceiling: if the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R, you get out. A report gap can be the case that tests it.

fixed before (variety rewrite)

questions.q: You bought the trigger close at 13.94, stop 13.42. It trades to 15.50. How many R is that?
questions.why: 3R. One R is the fill minus the stop. Divide the gain, the price minus the fill, by one R. That is where the first third comes off; FRO got there in 7 sessions.
questions.lesson_line: Count in R, not dollars. 3R is the first trim.
questions.simple: Divide the gain by the risk per share, the buy price minus the stop, and you get 3R.

deeper.trap: Judging a gain by its percent. The same percent gain is more R when the stop is close and fewer R when it is wide. Count in R, because the trim rules are written in R.

reasons: computed key

questions.q: Which grades higher?
choices: The rising 50-day above the 200
Equal; the line is what matters
The flat one; it is less stretched
The one under the 200; more upside
questions.why: The one over a rising 50-day that sits above the 200-day. Our card prefers that location and prefers to avoid a 50-day under the 200-day. The grade then sets the size: A and B setups at normal size, A+ sized up, B- or lower sized down.
questions.lesson_line: Same shape, two locations. Rising averages in the right order earn the better grade.

wrong.Equal; the line is what matters: The line is the trigger. Location grades the trade, and the grade sets the size.
wrong.The flat one; it is less stretched: Less stretched is not a grade. A 50-day under the 200-day is the location we prefer to avoid.
wrong.The one under the 200; more upside: Cheaper is not stronger. Our card prefers a rising 50-day over the 200-day, and prefers to avoid the reverse.

questions.story: Two Slingshots with the same drive and the same tidy pullback. One sits over a rising 50-day above the 200-day. The other sits over a flat 50-day that is under the 200-day.
questions.simple: The Slingshot over a rising 50-day above the 200-day grades higher, because that is the location our card prefers.

deeper.trap: The line is only the trigger. Two charts can share the same line and sit in very different places, and the place moves the grade, not the entry rule. LOW had its 50-day under its 200-day and was stopped on day 1.

reasons: rests on one card line (c12)
preference is a held decision (D-009)

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Sell; under 1R after 10 days
Hold; no stop hit in 10 days
Add; it is still above the line
Sell half and hold the rest
questions.why: Sell. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money. At 0.6R after 10 days this one has not resumed, and an untouched stop does not change the time stop.
questions.lesson_line: Ten days and nothing. The money has somewhere better to be.

wrong.Add; it is still above the line: No adding. And a trade that has done nothing in 10 days is not asking for more money.
wrong.Hold; no stop hit in 10 days: The stop is one exit. The time stop is another, and it fired.
wrong.Sell half and hold the rest: The time stop sells the trade, not part of it, freeing the money.

questions.story: Ten trading days after a Slingshot buy the trade sits at 0.6R, drifting sideways. The stop has not been touched.
questions.simple: Sell it, because a trade under 1R after 10 trading days is sold to free the money.

deeper.trap: Waiting because the stop has not hit. The stop and the time stop are two separate exits. Not being stopped out does not mean the trade is working.

reasons: a number in the owner's rulebook (C33)
rests on a rule that can change

questions.q: Three of the four failed Slingshots in our examples were stopped within two sessions, the stop doing its job.
questions.why: True. Three of the four failed Slingshots in our examples were stopped within two sessions. SRPT and LOW were stopped on day 1, PSX on day 2. PLTR was stopped on day 4, by a gap under the stop. The trigger day's low did not hold, which is what the stop under it is placed to detect.
questions.lesson_line: A Slingshot that fails usually fails fast. The tight stop is what makes that cheap.
questions.simple: True, because three of the four failures were stopped within two sessions, which is the stop doing its job.

deeper.trap: Four losses is a tiny sample. It shows how these failures looked, not how often a Slingshot fails, and this unit states no win rate. What it does show is the design: a stop a few cents under the trigger day's low gets you out fast, so a failure stays small.

reasons: one fact carries it, our own bars dossier

questions.q: Grade?
choices: Not orderly; pass on it
A+; the drive is huge
B; buy a half-size position
Orderly; under 2 ATR
questions.why: Pass. Orderly means three things. The whole pullback sits inside about 1.6 ATR. No red body is over 3.5% of price. No down day comes on volume above its 50-day average. This one fails all three: 1.85 ATR, a 4% red body, and above-average volume on that red day. Our card cut a choppy pullback like TCOM at 1.85 ATR. A huge drive does not excuse it.
questions.lesson_line: A big drive does not excuse a messy pullback. Orderly is a gate.

wrong.A+; the drive is huge: The drive is one row of the grade. The pullback fails the orderly test on every count.
wrong.B; buy a half-size position: Half of a messy pullback is still a messy pullback. Orderly is a gate, not a grade.
wrong.Orderly; under 2 ATR: The card's limit is about 1.6 ATR, not 2. This pullback is 1.85 ATR, and the 4% red body on above-average volume fails as well.

questions.story: A drive, then a pullback whose total range is 1.85 ATR, with one red candle body of 4% of price on above-average volume. Today it closes over the line.
questions.simple: Not orderly, so pass: the range is 1.85 ATR, over the 1.6 limit, and a 4% red body sits on above-average volume.

deeper.trap: A huge drive makes people forgive a messy pullback. The card treats orderly as a gate, not a grade: the whole pullback inside about 1.6 ATR, no red body over 3.5%, no down day on heavy volume. Count the three tests before you look at the drive.

reasons: rests on the criteria card's proposed 1.6 ATR and 3.5%
card lists choppy as both a gate and a B- row
fixed before

questions.q: Size?
choices: Sized down
Normal size
Sized up
No trade
questions.why: Sized down. A and B setups at normal size; A+ sized up; B- or lower sized down. Risk by grade puts B- or lower at 0.25% to 0.5%. Green means full risk per grade, so it does not lift a B-.
questions.lesson_line: The grade sets the size. A B- gets the smallest risk, 0.25% to 0.5%.

wrong.Normal size: Normal size is for A and B setups. B- is sized down.
wrong.No trade: A B- is not a skip. Our rule sizes it down, to 0.25% to 0.5% risk.

questions.story: Every gate passes, but on your read this Slingshot grades B-. The reading is Green.
questions.simple: A B- grade means a smaller size, even in a Green market, because the grade sets how much to risk.

deeper.trap: Green reads like permission to size up. It only means full risk per grade. A B- stays a B- in a Green market, so it stays sized down.

reasons: rests on the owner's grade and risk rules (D38, E49)
sizing by grade is a held decision (D-005)
fixed before: story corrected

questions.q: You buy as it trades over the line, on an R-based plan. Entry, stop and first trim?
choices: 62.40; stop 60.82; a third at 3R
62.40; stop 58.30; out at 2R
62.40; stop at the gap low; hold to 5R
62.40; stop 60.82; all out at 3R
questions.why: Market as it trades over the line, 62.40. The stop goes a few cents under the day's low, 60.82. A third comes off at 3R, another third at 5R, and the last third trails. That is one taught plan. A sell into a push of a few days is equally ours.
questions.lesson_line: Entry, stop, trim, trail. Write it before the trigger fires; execute it without a debate.

wrong.62.40; stop 58.30; out at 2R: That stop is nowhere near the day's low. And the R-based plan puts the first trim at 3R, not 2R.
wrong.62.40; stop at the gap low; hold to 5R: The gap low is a different level. The stop goes a few cents under the day's low, not at the gap low.
wrong.62.40; stop 60.82; all out at 3R: Entry and stop are right, the exit is not. The plan takes a third at 3R, another third at 5R, and trails the last third.

questions.story: A stock gapped up 9%, then rested three small red candles. Today it trades back over its line, and you buy at 62.40. The day's low so far is 60.85.
questions.simple: Buy at 62.40 as price trades over the line, stop a few cents under the day's low at 60.82, and a third off at 3R.

deeper.trap: Write the whole plan before the trigger fires: entry, stop, first trim, trail. The stop sets the size, so the distance to the stop decides how many shares you can buy. Then carry the plan out without a debate.

reasons: held decision D-003 (trigger order)
rests on rulebook E51, E57 and F62

questions.q: Slingshot?
choices: No; no drive to sling from
Yes; the shape is enough
Yes; a decisive close
No; four closes too few
questions.answer: No; no drive to sling from
questions.why: No. The drive comes first, and this stock never had one. Scot1and wants a stock that recently made a strong move. The shape and a decisive close cannot stand in for a drive.
questions.lesson_line: The shape without the drive is not a Slingshot. The drive comes first.

wrong.Yes; the shape is enough: The shape alone is not the setup. The drive comes first, and it is missing.
wrong.Yes; a decisive close: A decisive close is only the trigger. The drive has to come first.
wrong.No; four closes too few: Three closes is the minimum, and this pullback has four. The missing piece is the drive.

questions.story: A stock has gone sideways for four months: no gap, no strong move up, no big volume day. Then it closes four times under its 4-day line and closes decisively back over it.
questions.simple: No. The stock only went sideways, and a strong move up has to come before the pullback.

deeper.trap: Calling it a Slingshot because the shape looks right. The line, the closes and the decisive close are all there. With no drive first, it is only a wobble in a sideways stock.

reasons: rests on the drive-first line of our card (c44)
story has no strong move under any option of the held drive decision (D-106)

questions.q: The only time a Slingshot stop moves against you is the gap rule: the first 30-minute low on a gap-down day.
questions.why: True. The stop only moves up, never down or wider. The one exception is the gap rule: after a gap through the stop, the low of the first 30-minute bar is the new stop. It has a ceiling: if those 30 minutes take the loss past 2R, get out. The gap makes that call, not you.
questions.lesson_line: One exception, and it is not yours to choose. The gap decides, in 30 minutes.
questions.simple: True, because the stop only moves up, except on a gap through it, where the first 30-minute low is the new stop.

deeper.trap: Widening a stop by hand is a named mistake. The gap rule is different: it replaces a stop the market already traded through with a defined one, and it still has a ceiling. Do not stretch it to excuse an ordinary dip under your stop.

reasons: rests on rulebook A4 and B20

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Buy nothing; no setup, no trade
Buy the near one; it is Green
Buy it small, tight stop
Buy a weaker name that fires
questions.answer: Buy nothing; no setup, no trade
questions.why: Buy nothing. No setup, no trade; cash is a position. A mid-range close is not a decisive trigger, and a near-miss is a miss. Green is full risk per grade for a setup that passes; it does not create one.
questions.lesson_line: Green is permission, not an order. Wait for the one that passes every gate.

wrong.Buy the near one; it is Green: Green sets the size for a setup that passes. It does not create one.
wrong.Buy it small, tight stop: Small is a size, not a setup. Never force a trade to have something on.
wrong.Buy a weaker name that fires: We buy leaders, and a weaker name is still forcing a trade. Never force a trade to have something on.

questions.story: Earnings season, and the reading is Green. Your list shows no Slingshot that passes every gate. One is close, but its trigger closed mid-range.
questions.simple: Do nothing, because no Slingshot passes every gate and a near-miss is still a miss.

deeper.trap: A Green market feels like permission to act. It only sets the risk for setups that pass. Never force a trade to have something on.

reasons: rests on the owner's no-setup rule (D44)
fixed before: choice reworded

questions.q: You bought the trigger close at 66.08 with the stop at 64.04. Where is 5R?

questions.lesson_line: Know your 5R before the open. The second third comes off there.
questions.simple: One R is the buy price minus the stop, so 5R is the buy price plus five times that gap.

reasons: computed key

questions.q: What comes off now?
choices: Another 30; trail the last 30
Another 45; trail 15
The last 60, all of it
Nothing; await the 21-day
questions.why: Another 30, a third of the position. The first third came off at 3R, the second comes off at 5R, and you trail the last third. The trail is the 10-day for a fast mover or the 21-day for a steadier one.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, a third at 5R, then trail the rest.

wrong.Another 45; trail 15: A third of 90 is 30, not 45. The last third, 30 shares, trails.
wrong.The last 60, all of it: The plan keeps the last third on the trail, not out at 5R.
wrong.Nothing; await the 21-day: The trail starts after both trims. At 5R the second third comes off.

questions.story: You bought 90 shares of a Slingshot at the trigger close. You sold a third at 3R. Today the stock reaches 5R.

questions.q: Is today's close a Slingshot buy?

Yes; four closes under, then back over
Yes; heavy volume makes it a drive
No; it needs a gap open to count
questions.answer: No; a drive day is never the trigger

wrong.Yes; four closes under, then back over: That is only the pullback and the close back over. No drive came before it, so the shape has nothing to sling from.
wrong.No; it needs a gap open to count: A trigger that gaps up 2% or more is a named mistake. The card wants a trigger that opens less than 2% over the prior close.
wrong.Yes; heavy volume makes it a drive: Even if today counts as a drive day, the drive day is never the trigger. The drive has to come before the pullback.

questions.why: No. A Slingshot needs a drive before the pullback starts. Three flat months gave none. Today's surge is the first strong day, and the drive day is never the trigger. With no drive before the dip, there is nothing to sling from.
questions.lesson_line: A big day after a dip is not the drive. The drive has to come before the pullback.
questions.simple: No, because the drive has to come before the pullback, and today's surge cannot be both the drive and the buy.
